items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I was playing up to the West End last week and Howard started this way back

ctx.x: But as I said before, I think the record companies are the cause of this. I mean, Coltrane was turned around, everybody was turned around because every record company you go to to record, "what can you do different?" There's nothing different musically. I mean I hear just like sensationalism, if you want it. You don't have to learn your instrument to do that.

I was playing up to the West End last week and Howard started this way back -- in fact, there was a young fellow named Buddy Terry, fine saxophone player. But I guess in keeping with the trend, you know, they get off onto this avant garde thing. And we were playing so he played -- I played my chorus and then he got up and played and he went into this thing. And so after he finished I just jumped and did the same thing and it broke up the house, you know.

So last week when I was over there we were playing "Back Home in Indiana". And I just got up and I played about ten choruses. And then on the last chorus I went (makes gargling noise) you know, like I hear them do. And everybody just went wild. I mean it's just that even Bill ran up, you know. But I don't know, I guess this is the age of emotion and everybody wants to get excited about something instead of relaxing back and listening to a nice something -- music, you know.
